title: I4MS (phase 4) - uptake of digital game changers
description: PULSATE is a part of the Horizon 2020 programme called I4MS funded by the European Commission with the goal to accelerate the design, development and uptake of advanced digital technologies by the European Manufacturing industry to empower personalised products and to facilitate cost-effective small-scale production. One of these digitalization technologies that PULSATE project is focused on is Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM). To boost and support the uptake, PULSATE will select and support end-users (Adopters) SMEs and Slightly bigger companies that are willing to implement Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technologies into their environment. To enable this, PULSATE project brings together a strong consortium comprising six competence centres (AIMEN, FTMC, MTC, SINTEF, Fraunhofer and CEA) with high-level expertise in LBAAM and digitisation, the European Photonics Industry Consortium (EPIC) to support the acceleration of EU innovative scale-up initiatives, and two highly innovative SMEs (CLESGO & Fundingbox) to establish and support the Digital Agora platform, maintain a Marketplace of digital services and to manage the mechanisms of financial support to selected companies and the connection with DIHs across all Europe. Through the 2 nd Open Call for Adopters, PULSATE will select up to 18 Adopter SMEs/Slightly Bigger companies that represent high-potential business use cases for implementation of LBAAM technology in their processes, products and business models. Selected Adopters will take part in a 3-month support programme between january and april 2024, through which they will receive: - Up to €25 000 as a lump sum - Mentorship from PULSATE Consortium partners in LBAAM feasibility assessment that will allow Adopters to confirm Technical and Business Feasibility for the implementation of LBBAM technology in their environment.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Applications must be submitted via https://pulsate-adopters.fundingbox.com . The selection of the open call proposals will be carried out in a four-step process: Step 1 will check the proposals against eligibility criteria. Step 2 will involve external evaluation to assess the proposal according to the criteria. Step 3 will involve the PULSATE consortium to prioritise the proposals based on the external evaluation results and the objectives of the PULSATE project. Step 4 legal check before finalists are invited to sign the Sub Grant Agreement. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 4. Applicants eligibility PULSATE is looking for End-user / Technology Adopter companies that are interested in the implementation of LBAAM technology into their environment that will enhance the activities of the manufacturing industry. Adopters should represent high-potential business Use Cases for implementation of Laser-Based Advanced and Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technology in their processes, products and business models. Applications can be submitted by only ONE company that has the status of SMEs or a Slightly Bigger company and is legally established in one of the eligible countries. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 3.

title: Interoperable and smart homes and grids
description: The selected applicants will participate in the InterConnect Support Programme, with a duration of maximum 7 months, split into 3 stages: 1st STAGE: Specification & Development Plan (1 month) Up to ten (10) selected beneficiaries will be invited to participate in a Welcome Event where the Technical and Business Mentors will be allocated to each Project. Beneficiaries will have (1 month) to define ‘Specification and Development Plan’ for the Energy Application, with support of their mentors that will include KPIs and Deliverables that will be used to evaluate the projects’ performance and define the payment schedule. At the end of Stage 1 a ‘Selection Day’ will take place. Projects will be invited to pitch their solutions in front of the ‘Selection Committee’. Up to seven (7) beneficiaries with the highest score will be selected to continue in the programme, the rest will finish their participation in the Support Programme. 2nd STAGE: Development & Integration (3 months) Up to seven (7) beneficiaries will be selected to develop the different interoperable components and services and make the necessary integration for pre-testing and validation of the Energy Application ecosystem. During the duration of this stage beneficiaries will have access to Specialized and Technical Mentors that will provide support to the different activities. By the end of this period an intermediate report will be delivered by the beneficiaries to demonstrate the achieved progress and results. 3rd STAGE: Demonstration in the field (3 months) Up to seven (7) beneficiaries will validate and demonstrate the Energy Application ecosystem in a set of preselected consumers that will use the developed set of services and show how consumers can take an active role in supporting the grid resiliency whilst potentiating energy savings. The performance will be evaluated through the presented results on the established KPIs. A final report will be delivered where the results achieved will be presented as well as relevant lessons learned for the CERF. All data concerning the results produced during the demonstration period will have to be collected by the beneficiaries and made available to the EC or the project management for auditing purposes. Funding per stage: 1st stage: ‘Specification & Development Plan’ - up to 10,000.00€ per beneficiary 2nd stage: ‘Development & Integration’- up to 45,000.00€ per beneficiary 3rd stage: ‘Demonstration in the field’ - up to 45,000.00€ per beneficiary
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The Open Call will be supporting projects for demonstrators of energy applications in up to seven different EU member states, throughout seven months. The participants will have to define: a suitable Specification & Development Plan, the Development & Integration of interoperable components and services, Demonstration in the field of use of the energy applications involving grid stakeholder and consumers. The InterConnect project will provide interoperability tools and frameworks to be used and improved by the Open Call participants. The InterConnect project is looking for highly motivated and skilled candidates able to engage an ecosystem of grid stakeholders and consumers to demonstrate the ability to contribute to grid resiliency whilst supporting energy efficiency and cost reduction aligned with the Common European Reference Framework (CERF). Submission through the application form is available here . The selection of the open call proposals will be carried out in a three-step process. Step one: first check on proposals’ eligibility. Step two: ranking of proposals by external evaluators. Step three: selection of the final list of participants by the InterConnect Selection Committee. The eligible participants of this program are SMEs (including start-ups), mid-caps or large companies that are registered in one of the eligible countries. Participants registered in any EU member states , are eligible to participate, however only projects to be demonstrated in the countries listed below , can be selected for funding. Eligible countries for demonstrators: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary*, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Project demonstrators in Portugal, the Netherlands, Italy, and Greece are excluded from this open call, as InterConnect has already established use cases being demonstrated in these countries. Only one project from each eligible country will be selected and funded as part of the open call. For further information see the Guide of Applicants (GfA) . *Following the Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/2506, as of 16th December 2022, no legal commitments can be signed with Hungarian public interest trusts established under Hungarian Act IX of 2021 or any entity they maintain. Affected entities may continue to apply to calls for proposals. However, in case the Council measures are not lifted, such entities are not eligible to participate in any funded role (beneficiaries, affiliated entities, subcontractors, recipients of financial support to third parties). In this case, co-applicants will be invited to remove or replace that entity and/or to change its status into associated partner. Tasks and budget may be redistributed accordingly.

title: Methods for bridging reality gaps
description: The BattleVerse 1st Open Call aims to support the development and validation of innovative technological solutions that contribute to advanced mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence related environments. Selected applicants will implement a six-month experiment, developing and demonstrating their proposed solution and assessing its potential contribution to the BattleVerse ecosystem. Proposals shall address one of the following three technical topics: Topic 1: LLMs for strategic decision-making, symbolic reasoning, game theory and planning under uncertainty. Experiments under this topic will explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI-based approaches to support strategic decision-making and mission planning, including symbolic reasoning, game-theoretic modelling, planning under uncertainty and human-in-the-loop approaches. Topic 2: Multi-physics simulation capabilities for multi-domain defence environments. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate simulation approaches capable of modelling complex operational environments and interactions across multiple warfare domains. Topic 3: Distributed AI for autonomous systems (UxVs) with for coordinated swarm operations. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate how autonomous systems powered by machine learning and distributed AI can support coordinated multi-UxV operations in complex operational environments. Across the three topics, proposed experiments should demonstrate a clear technological contribution, a credible implementation approach and the potential to advance the capabilities of the BattleVerse simulation environment. Experiments are expected to achieve at least TRL 5 by the end of the six-month implementation period. Selected beneficiaries will also have access to targeted coaching and guidance activities provided by the BattleVerse consortium. These activities will support applicants in addressing relevant technical challenges related to the development, integration, testing and validation of their solutions. The selected beneficiaries will remain fully responsible for the implementation and delivery of their experiments.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The BattleVerse project , a European Defence Fund Development Action co-funded under grant agreement No 101224034, foresees the provision of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP), also referred to as Cascade Funding, to support innovative experiments contributing to the objectives of the project. The BattleVerse 1 st Open Call is designed to support innovative experiments contributing to the development and validation of advanced technologies for mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence-related environments. The Open Call primarily targets SMEs, including start-ups , and will provide selected beneficiaries with financial support to implement experiments over a period of six months. The Open Call covers three technical topics designed to advance next-generation defence simulation capabilities. Applicants are invited to propose innovative solutions in AI-enabled decision support (including Machine Learning, LLMs, strategic decision-making and human-in-the-loop AI), advanced modelling and simulation (including MSaaS, Digital Twins and multi-domain simulation environments), or autonomous defence systems (including unmanned vehicles, distributed AI and swarm operations). Proposal applications must be submitted exclusively via the BattleVerse Submission Portal . Experiments may be implemented by a single SME or start-up , or by an eligible consortium of up to three beneficiaries . Participation of entities other than SMEs, including RTOs and academic institutions, may only be accepted where no suitable SME is available to provide the specific capacity or expertise required for the successful implementation of the experiment, and such participation must be duly justified in the proposal. The proposal must be written in English in all mandatory parts to be eligible. The project description shall not exceed 15 pages as indicated in the Proposal Template. Only a proposal included in the Proposal Template will be reviewed by Evaluators. The evaluation will be performed per topics. Applications submitted by email, post, or any means other than the one described above will not be considered. The assessment of the Call will follow transparent evaluation criteria, lump-sum funding modalities, and strict governance procedures in full compliance with the corresponding EDF's Model Grant Agreement . The eligibility criteria applicable to the BattleVerse 1st Open Call reflect the relevant requirements of the European Defence Fund and the specific conditions established for Financial Support to Third Parties. To be eligible, applicants must: Be a legal private entity qualifying as Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise as defined by the European Commission . Entities other than SMEs may participate only in duly justified cases where the specific capacity or expertise required for the experiment cannot be provided by an available eligible SME. Applicants must be legal entities established in any of the countries eligible for this open call: A EU27 Member State or Norway or Ukraine. This follows country eligibility criteria under the EDF as well as the Commission Implementing Decision of 29 January 2025 (C(2025) 568 final EDF-funded activities are subject to specific ownership and control requirements in accordance with Article 9 EDF Regulation. To be eligible for this Call, entities must be established in an EU Member State, Norway or Ukraine. Applicants controlled by an entity from a non-eligible country will be excluded. Applicants must comply with all eligibility criteria defined in this Guide for Applicants , including requirements related to geographical scope, ownership control, security requirements, conflict of interest and data protection. These conditions are aligned with the applicable rules of the European Defence Fund, tailored to the reality of financial support to third parties. Applicants must have the know-how, qualifications and resources to successfully implement the projects and contribute their share (including sufficient experience in projects of comparable size and nature). Applicants to this Call must submit the Ownership Control Declaration . Comply with ethics requirements as defined in Article 7 of EDF Regulation . Comply with security requirements of the Call. Comply with financial capacity requirements of the Call. Comply with any other specificity of the Call. Not have any conflict of interest with BattleVerse consortium partners.

title: Ammunition, missiles and other explosive weapons
description: Expected Impact: The results of the activities should contribute to support common procurement, leading to strengthening the cooperation among Member States and associated countries, as well as to greater interoperability. Furthermore, they should contribute to the building up of strategic stockpile of ammunition, missiles, including their components, or to the increase of existing ones, as well as to the development of low-cost unmanned systems for guided strikes adapted to modern warfare scenarios. Objective: This topic aims at actions supporting the common procurement of ammunition (including small arms ammunition, tank and anti-tank ammunitions, artillery ammunition, guided ammunitions), missiles (all types of missiles) and other explosive weapons (including hand grenade, land and naval mines, mortar, rockets, unmanned systems (aerial, ground, surface and underwater vehicles controlled remotely or operating autonomously using advanced software and sensors) able to perform guided strikes (including attack or kamikaze drones, FPV loitering munitions), torpedoes), or parts thereof, contributing to replenishment of stocks. Scope: Common procurement actions under this topic shall consist of activities related to the cooperation of legal entities in the procurement of ammunition, missiles, and other explosive weapons, at any point in the life cycle of such defence products, including for the purpose of establishing, managing and maintaining defence industrial readiness pools. Where relevant (e.g. unmanned systems for guided strikes), procurement contracts are expected to include provisions allowing to rapidly upgrade the procured systems based on evolving lessons identified from the battlefield. To achieve the expected impact, the estimated value of a common procurement proposed for actions under this topic shall be of at least EUR 20 000 000 aiming to commonly procure defence products to fill the capability gaps and reinforce cooperation among Member States and associated countries. The procurement shall be based on a binding agreement to be signed by the participating Member States and associated countries with a procurement agent appointed by those Member States and associated countries. Such procurement agent may be contracting authorities of Member States or associated countries, the European Defence Agency (EDA), a Structure for European Armament Programme (SEAP) or other international organisation, including the Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation (OCCAR) or the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). The cooperation shall be newly created in the context of the application to the call topic or based on an existing framework, provided that the activities under such cooperation framework did not start before 5 March 2024 and have not been completed before the signature of the grant agreement. Eligible actions are common procurement of systems, parts thereof or variants of systems. The common procurement can be organised as a framework contract. Actions shall be completed no later than 31 December 2033.

title: Counter-drone systems
description: Expected Impact: The results of the activities should contribute to support common procurement, leading to strengthening the cooperation among Member States and associated countries, as well as to greater interoperability. Furthermore, they should contribute to the replenishment of depleted stockpiles of counter-drone systems, to the increase of existing stockpiles or to establishment of defence industrial readiness pool, as well as to the development and reinforcement of counter-drone solutions as drones are being increasingly perceived as a pressing threat. Objective: This topic aims at actions supporting the common procurement of integrated systems (e.g. VSHORAD or SHORAD) or parts thereof (including sensors, kinetic or non-kinetic effectors - including direct energy weapons -, command and control solutions) to counter unmanned aerial, ground, surface or underwater vehicles, including those controlled remotely or operating autonomously using advanced software and sensors. Scope: Common procurement actions under this topic shall consist of activities related to the cooperation of legal entities in the procurement of integrated counter-drone systems or parts thereof, at any point in the life cycle of such defence products, including for the purpose of establishing, managing and maintaining defence industrial readiness pools. Procurements contracts are expected to include provisions allowing to upgrade quickly the counter-drone systems based on the evolving lessons identified from the battlefield. To achieve the expected impact, the estimated value of a common procurement proposed for actions under this topic shall be at least EUR 20 000 000 aiming to commonly procure defence products to fill the capability gaps and reinforce cooperation among Member States and associated countries. The procurement shall be based on a binding agreement to be signed by the participating Member States and associated countries with a procurement agent appointed by those Member States and associated countries. Such procurement agent may be contracting authorities of Member States or associated countries, the European Defence Agency (EDA), a Structure for European Armament Programme (SEAP) or other international organisation, including the Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation (OCCAR) or the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). The cooperation shall be newly created in the context of the application to the call topic or based on an existing SENSITIVE EN 4 EN framework, provided that the activities under such cooperation framework did not start before 5 March 2024 and have not been completed before the signature of the grant agreement. Eligible actions are common procurement of systems, parts thereof or variants of those. The common procurement can be organised as a framework contract. Actions shall be completed no later than 31 December 2033.
